newsitem.title: SPAIN: Banesto says no news on Urbis, shares soar.
newsitem.headline: Banesto says no news on Urbis, shares soar.

text.p: Sources at Banesto, whose Corporacion Banesto sold five percent of real estate group Urbis last week, said they had no fresh news on the firm to account for the strong rise in Urbis shares on Wednesday.
At 1340 GMT, Urbis was up 30 pesetas, or 2.03 percent, to 1,505 pesetas in heavy trade. The Ibex-35 blue chip index was up 1.32 percent 7,157.20.

"There (is) nothing new, but a lot of people have been calling us asking us what's going on," a Banesto source said. "I would simply reiterate our 1,900 pesetas target price and the fact that it's normal for the shares to rise given the forecasts for the company."
The Banesto group still has a 66-percent stake in Urbis after last week's sale.
But analysts said the shares were overvalued based on fundamentals.
Juan Ramon Correas, analyst at Ahorro Corporacion Financiera, said Urbis was now well over his target price of 1,200 pesetas per share based on the firm's net asset value.
"Four months ago, it was my star stock. But (the shares) started the year at 500 pesetas, and they've now tripled. The stock has now caught up on all of its (previous) underperformance," he said.
But a June 30 research note by Banesto Bolsa, the brokerage arm that carried out the placement, it based a recommendation for Urbis on the expected benefits of a pick-up in the economy.

"The weighting of (real estate) development in Urbis' business will increase from 72 percent at present to 93 percent in 2001, boosting recurrent income...In the current climate of economic recovery, Urbis is in an unbeatable position to take advantage of the pick-up in demand, which is a result of lower mortgage rates," the note said.
